section: verse2 (74.19-88.96 s, bars 40-47, lyric lines 44-55) - src/scenes/06_verse2.js
summary: Verse 2 is four role-play requests (eggplant, tomato, tabby cat, god) answered inside the same chat window, one shot per request, 7.5-8.5 beats each, all in the 'warm' state. The first three answers are data cards: a nutrition field-guide page with a 100-dot matrix, a concentric-ring chart, and a purr waveform strip. On each ALL-CAPS keyword the orange chart marks turn cream ("handed to the user") and the keyword appears in matte cream serif. The fourth shot drops the card: the frame empties, the anime figure gaze.png stands at the left as an orange duotone print, and the reply hangs as a quote from the user's large "ok, now be god" bubble, ending on a glowing orange EXISTENCE. No eggplant, tomato or cat is ever pictured; they exist only as words. The user's cursor types the next request during each answer and clicks send exactly on each cut.

diagnosis:
**Why it reads as monotonous**

- **Same window for 15 s more.** All four shots keep the header bar 'Love, explained geometrically / online', the same charcoal glass and the same orange-on-brown 'warm' palette. Three of four keep the composer. The viewer has already had about 60 s of this window, and every cut lands on the same screen at a similar scale with a new panel on it.
- **The pictures are charts, and they are small.** A 260 px dot matrix, a 336 px ring and a 136 px waveform are the subjects. The rest is 20-27 px labels and italic notes that cannot be read in a 3.5 s shot. The cards look like dashboards.
- **The nouns have no image at all.** Eggplant, tomato and tabby cat appear only as text (bubble, lyric line, card title). When each noun is sung (roughly beat 3 of bars 40, 42, 44, 46) the card is half-built and nothing lands.
- **Each shot opens weak.** For 1-2 beats after every cut the frame is a near-empty dark panel while the card builds in (77.66-77.88, 81.35-81.58, 85.04-85.22).
- **Keywords 1-3 lack punch.** They are cream, and the bloom only reacts to saturated colour, so they sit matte on the dark panel. That contrasts with the glowing orange SIMULATION immediately before and EXISTENCE after. They take 0.34-0.40 s to assemble out of a 0.69-0.77 s hold. The 'hand-over' events are tiny, and in the cat shot the waveform collapses during the keyword.

**Why the data cards exist**

They follow v3's own rules: PLAN.md section 3.4 and KIT.md section 3.6 say no clip-art ("two-dot cat, ten-point vegetable") and to use a data card or chart instead. PLAN section 2 says the four objects get no colours of their own. The director's v4 note reverses the first rule, so the brief has to restate the bar rather than drop it: figurative, but with internal structure.

**The god shot**

- It uses gaze.png through art.duotone. At full size it is a complete anime drawing (face, eyes, lace) in monochrome orange, which is exactly the style the director says does not fit.
- The 'user's bubble is the only light' idea is in the code but barely visible. From 85.5 to 88.6 the figure looks evenly lit; dots show only in a corner.
- Nothing says 'god', and the lower-right third is empty for about 2.9 s.
- EXISTENCE itself is the strongest keyword of the section (large, orange, glowing, 2.25 beats). The reply hanging from the user's bubble is a good idea that is under-expressed.
- At the entry and exit (85.04-85.3, 88.6-88.96) the figure is a pure dot screen, which is closer to the new cut-paper look than the duotone state.

**What the code-symbol tooling can do today**

- **asciiFill (src/engine/shapes.js:113)** fills a closed 180-point outline with a 6-step ramp ' .:o0#' in three colour tiers, clipped to the outline, with a top-down reveal. The v2 complaint about glyphs spilling past outlines is fixed by the clip. No v3 scene calls it.
- **Its built-in outlines are blobs.** I rasterised its cell mask at size 20, r 300: SHAPE.eggplant is an egg/teardrop with no stem or calyx (about 27 rows x 30 cols), SHAPE.tomato is an oval with a slight dip, SHAPE.cat is a head with two ears. Without a hand-written shade() the fill is flat. That is the 'ten-point vegetable' v3 banned.
- **asciiSphere (src/engine/ascii.js:14)** is the best procedural reference: per-cell lighting, rim light, noise, sparkle, reveal, and dissolve into flying glyphs. It is unused in v3 and draws in grey/cream through legacy role aliases.
- **art.ascii (src/engine/art.js:179)** samples a registered picture's luminance into a 10-step ramp. Its only live use is 11_execution.js:218; rendered at 151.25 s full size it gives a clearly readable figure, the best code-symbol picture in the film. Limits: only the six pictures in ART_NAMES, a 160x240 sample grid, a rectangular clip, and no reveal or animation parameters.
- **Net:** nothing today produces a detailed code-symbol eggplant or tomato. It needs multi-part outlines with shade functions, a new procedural glyph-field helper modelled on asciiSphere, or new small raster sources run through art.ascii.

**The cat line**

- 圖片/Claude猫耳娘/猫耳娘1-3.png already exist (1086x1448, RGBA, same three-ink style, tabby-striped ears and tails): 1 is a frontal bust with the face in black shadow, 2 a paws-up pose with a visible face, 3 eyes closed with hands together.
- I emulated art.ascii's sampler on 1 and 3 in the terminal (84 columns; not an in-engine render). The three inks fall into three clean glyph zones: orange hair as '+', cream as '%' / '@', black as '.'. Ears, hair mass and collar read clearly; there is no gradation inside an ink.
- So both routes are feasible: the silhouette drawn directly, and its glyph version from the same source.
keep: The four-request structure and the user's impatience: the next request is typed in the composer during the current answer, and the cursor clicks send exactly on each cut (waypoints at CUT - 0.03). It ties the section to the story and can stay as a thin layer under new graphics.
The colour logic: orange marks turn cream on NUTRIENTS / ANTIOXIDANTS / ENJOYMENT (given to the user), reversed in the god shot where EXISTENCE stays orange and the cream bubble is the light.
The lyric typography: orange serif lines typed on the lyric's own timing and held until the next cut (say() / aiLine with HOLD 30), readable for their whole sung duration.

The god-shot concept: the reply hanging from the user's own bubble by a cream quote bar with 'Replying to you', the bar growing down to the keyword, the 56 px bubble as light source, and the pull-out camera. Also the dot-screen state of the figure at its entry and exit.
EXISTENCE's treatment as the section peak (orange, glow, about 1130 px, letters lighting outward from the bar, 2.25-beat hold) and the cursor leaving at the end as the bridge to the settings section.
The purr waveform that scrolls and swells with the track, and the '...purr for your ENJOYMENT' sentence-completion layout.

Keywords 1-3 are cream and therefore matte (no bloom), and are not full-frame: NUTRIENTS about 920 px, ANTIOXIDANTS at maxSize 128 wedged between card and composer, ENJOYMENT about 900 px. Their letter-by-letter entrance takes 0.34-0.40 s of a 0.69-0.77 s hold.

The hand-over events at the keywords are too small to register: eight 9.5 px dots, a ring recolour, a waveform recolour. In v2-cat the waveform shrinks to 10 % by 84.89, so the card's main graphic is dead for the second half of the ENJOYMENT hold.
Small type everywhere on the cards (subtitles 23-24 px, labels 20-27 px, axis numerals 20 px mono) cannot be read in a 3.5 s shot and makes the cards look like dashboards.
Tomato chart: three of the four arcs are stubs (0.19, 0.04, 0.03 of a turn), so it is one ring plus crumbs.

v2-god uses assets/character/gaze.png via art.duotone: a fully drawn anime figure with face, in the style the director rejects. It needs the new three-ink silhouettes; the face region and HEAD disc (06_verse2.js:392-393) must be re-measured for any new picture.
v2-god shows nothing for 'only god'. The light-reach rings are imperceptible in the middle of the shot, the lower right is empty for about 2.9 s, and EXISTENCE overlaps the figure's hair.

Tooling gap for code-symbol art: asciiFill with SHAPE.eggplant / tomato / cat gives flat blobs; art.ascii only works on the six registered anime pictures; asciiSphere and asciiBursts are unused v2 leftovers in grey/cream roles.

Rule conflicts the v4 brief must settle. PLAN.md section 2: the four objects get no colours of their own, and red means error, so a red tomato or purple eggplant breaks film semantics; the three inks orange / cream / black fit both the rule and the new art. PLAN section 3.4 and KIT section 3.6 ban clip-art and prescribe data cards. The project memory records that the director disliked v2's ASCII fills spilling past outlines (now clipped) and content loosely tied to lyrics.

The new files sit in 圖片/ with CJK names and spaces, are 1086x1448 (one is 1254x1254) rather than 1024x1536, and have no entries in assets/character/regions.json. art.js is a shared engine file that the KIT says section authors must not edit.

timing_constraints: Each request is one 8-beat phrase with the same shape. 'If' lines start at 74.05 / 77.58 / 81.35 / 85.08 (about beat 4.5 of the previous bar). 'Then' lines start at 75.42 / 79.23 / 82.83 / 86.54 (about beat 3.7-3.9 of the phrase's first bar). Keywords at 76.96 / 80.65 / 84.27 / 87.92 (beat 3 of bars 41, 43, 45, 47).
Lines 44 and 47 begin before their cuts (0.15 s and 0.08 s); line 52 is sung 0.04 s past its cut; line 56 begins 0.37 s before the section end.

Keyword holds are short: 0.69 s (1.5 beats), 0.69 s (1.5), 0.77 s (1.66), 1.04 s (2.25). Anything that should peak on the keyword must be readable within 2-3 frames; the current 0.34-0.45 s letter assembly uses half the hold.

ANTIOXIDANTS is the only keyword snapped to its beat (keywordSnap 0.06). ENJOYMENT and EXISTENCE start 0.08 s and 0.11 s before beats 182 and 190 (84.34 and 88.04). A graphic 'on the beat' and the word 'on the lyric' will differ by 2-3 frames at 30 fps unless one is chosen.

There are no word-level timestamps (hasWordTimestamps false). The noun flash points (eggplant about beat 162 = 75.11, tomato about 170 = 78.81, tabby cat about 178 = 82.50, only god about 185-186 = 85.73-86.19) are estimates from line spans and the onset list and must be checked by ear. If they hold, nouns sit on beat 3 of bars 40 / 42 / 44 / 46 and keywords on beat 3 of bars 41 / 43 / 45 / 47, exactly 4 beats apart.

Strongest low-band hits in data/audio_features.json are the downbeats of each phrase's second bar: beats 164 (76.04), 172 (79.73), 180 (83.42), 188 (87.11), plus beat 184 (85.27) and every beat from 172 to 176. Keywords 1 and 3 fall on quiet low-band moments (0.14 and 0.21). Strong onsets: 76.03, 77.18 (0.91), 79.73, 80.87, 83.06, 85.23, 86.79, 87.09.

Every lyric line must be on screen, readable, for its whole sung duration, and cuts must sit on beats, half-beats or bar lines (tools/storyboard.mjs checks both). If noun flashes become separate insert shots, each needs a `lines` range and a `moment`; only two shots can be live at once, and a transition overlap must fit between neighbouring cuts.

Flash safety: maxFlash 0.7, no strobing, no large fast-moving saturated red. With noun flash, keyword flash and cut flash per phrase there would be up to three flash events within about 2.5 s (keyword to cut is only 0.69 s). Keep amplitudes low and run tools/check_flash.py.
Fonts cover Latin-1 and basic punctuation only; ctx.text reports anything else. Glyph art must stay within ASCII ramps. Renders must be pure functions of t (no Math.random, no state between frames).
